text:
Gillespie had 3 state-licensed child care sites in 2025, state data shows
According to the Illinois Department of Children and Family Services, Gillespie was home to three licensed child care facilities in 2025.
Two of these were classified as group day care homes, making up 66.7%, while one was a family child care home at 33.3%.
Child care providers in Gillespie typically care for children from birth up to age 12.
All Gillespie facilities offer services in English, which is supported across providers in the area.
Illinois counted a total of 8,602 licensed child care facilities across the state in 2025.
The U.S. Department of Health and Human Services has frozen certain federal child care and family assistance funds for California, Colorado, Minnesota, New York and Illinois because of concerns regarding fraud and misuse, the agency said Jan. 6. Nearly $2.4 billion in Child Care and Development Fund grants, $7.35 billion in Temporary Assistance for Needy Families funds and $869 million in Social Services Block Grants are impacted, requiring states to supply documentation prior to releasing payments.
Illinois Gov. J.B. Pritzker called the action “wrong and cruel” and said Illinois may contest the freeze, pointing out that the state already has anti‑fraud policies in place.
State officials said the freeze could affect around 100,000 families and more than 152,000 children who use the Child Care Assistance Program, as well as funding for thousands of licensed child care providers and 275 human service agencies.
